key_insight: Encoder–decoder operator learning can be analyzed resolution-independently by passing to a limiting kernel, so generalization and regularization effects can be separated from encoding effects.
engineering_relevance: This gives practical error and complexity guidance for building scalable operator-learning models from discretized data, including neural network and kernel-based encoder–decoder systems.
method: Model the encoded data with a matrix-valued kernel that induces an operator-valued kernel on the original function spaces.
Prove convergence of the induced kernels to a limiting kernel via operator-norm convergence of their integral operators.
Derive upper and lower error bounds for regularized SGD and extend the analysis to encoder–decoder networks through the limiting NTK.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports upper and lower convergence/error bounds, including terms of order t^{-θ} and T^{-θ′}, plus polynomial parameter and sample complexity guarantees under algebraically decaying encoding errors.
watch_item: The bounds depend on how quickly encoding errors decay, so coarse discretizations or slow-decaying encodings may dominate performance and limit the practical benefit of the theory.
paper_title: Resolution-Independent Analysis of Encoder--Decoder Operator Learning via Limiting Kernels
